narrative: The model estimated a 43.0% probability that you would represent a bad credit risk, and under the lending rule applied, that risk level led to denial. The second most influential factor was your checking-account status. A balance of 0–200 DM pushed toward bad credit; this is less typical than having no overdraft, which describes 59.2% of approved applicants. The third most influential factor was your credit history. Although the requested amount helped your case, the checking-account position and credit-history profile raised risk enough that the overall assessment remained in the bad-risk range used for denial. Before reapplying, ask the lender whether a manual review or lower-risk product is possible, focus on maintaining a positive checking-account balance, and build a clearer record of repaid credit so future applications show stronger repayment evidence.
